title: What is known about 1RB1LA_1RC1RE_1RD0RD_1LA1RC_1RF0LE_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LA_1RC1RE_1RD0RD_1LA1RC_1RF0LE_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Right of the start the tape is a row of blocks u^n (u = 101011) separated by short markers. Each block is about four times as long as the one before it, and all of them grow linearly in the number of trips of the head, the largest by about 3 words every 25 trips and each smaller one four times slower; from time to time the smallest blocks are rebuilt and a new block appears (four blocks at 3·107 steps, five at 6·107). Lean proves the crossing of a block in state D, in both of its forms. No halt in 3·108 steps; the markers, which act like digits, are not worked out yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 48,282 cells have been visited and 37,278 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Crossing a block
claims.text: From L D> (101011)^n R the machine reaches L (111110)^n D> R in 6n steps, and from L D> (111110)^n R it reaches L (101011)^n D> R, for all n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: Blocks in the ratio 1 : 4 : 16 : ...
claims.text: The lengths of the long blocks (at least five words) at records of the head at the right end: [5, 20, 83, 345] at step 3.5·10<sup>6</sup>, [16, 67, 271, 1,095] at 3.4·10<sup>7</sup>, [5, 22, 91, 364, 1,470] at 6.1·10<sup>7</sup>, [11, 46, 184, 739, 2,970] at 2.5·10<sup>8</sup>. Between samples the largest block gains 375 words and each smaller one about a quarter of what the next one gains.

claims.title: A counter in the markers
claims.text: The markers between the blocks (such as a^4 u 1^4, a^7, a 1^6 a^4, with a = 10) cycle through a few shapes; the 1 : 4 rates suggest that each marker is a base-4 digit that moves the next block on by one word per cycle.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The only halting transition is F reading 1.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine builds a row of blocks, each about four times as long as the one before, that grow together like the hands of a clock running at speeds 1, 4, 16, ...

facts.text: No halt; five blocks, the largest of about 3,300 words.
Crossing a block in D is proved in Lean for every length.
Ratio of the growth rates of neighbouring blocks.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493).
After 109 steps the tape spans 48,282 cells (59 left of the start, 35,382 right), with a density of 1s of 0.772.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Blocks four times apart
html: Right of the start the tape is a row of blocks of the word u = 101011 with short markers between them. The long blocks at some records of the head at the right end:

Neighbouring blocks are about four times apart and grow at rates four times apart. Between 3.4·107 and 6.1·107 steps a fifth block appeared and the small ones were rebuilt. Lean proves that a block is crossed in state D in either of its two forms (cross_u, cross_u').

sections.heading: What the markers do
html: The markers cycle through a few shapes and seem to act as base-4 digits, each moving the next block on. The only halting transition is F reading 1. Working out the markers would turn the run into a counter whose behaviour could be followed much further, or proved.

summary: Right of the start the tape is a row of blocks of the word 101011, each about four times the one before, all growing in step; from time to time a new smallest block appears. Only partly analysed; open.
